title: frugal-prefill-orchestrator-and-quant-telemetry
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Large tenants with volatile traffic were incurring unnecessary token costs due to conservative prefill settings and broad quantization rollouts. This change introduces a Frugal Prefill Orchestrator (FPO) that combines short-horizon workload forecasts, tenant-level warmup lanes, and quantization guidance to reduce unit econ while preserving tail latency SLOs. Motivation: give operators a single place to reason about prefill budgets and quantized-serving rollouts, and provide a dry-run simulator so customers and SREs can validate cost/latency tradeoffs before enabling defaults. What this PR does: - Add a Prefill Orchestrator that computes per-tenant prefill budgets from recent traffic shapes and heatmap-derived cold-start probabilities. - Add a Quant Guidance API that recommends quant profiles (fp16/8bit/ptq) per model + tenant segment and can emit rollback signals when quality drift is detected. - Wire telemetry enrichment so the Console can show estimated per-tenant token savings and projected latency regressions when a quant profile or prefill policy is applied. - Add rwctl subcommand (rwctl prefill dry-run) to simulate a tenant rollout with synthetic request traces. - Add safety gates: conservative initial budget, canary rollout by tenant cohort, automatic fallback to full-precision if hallucination metrics or eval regressions cross thresholds. - Add unit and integration tests and a small load test harness used by CI. Checklist: [x] core orchestrator implementation; [x] telemetry + console enrichment; [x] rwctl CLI dry-run; [x] unit/integration tests; [x] docs draft. Related: Linear ENG-3245, ENG-3301. Risk: medium — changes affect routing and quant selection logic. Revert plan: the orchestrator can be disabled via a feature flag and a server-side kill switch that restores previous prefill defaults and quant profiles.
commits: init: add prefill orchestrator core and interfaces
telemetry: enrich batch/prefill metrics and tags (tenant_id, forecast_bucket)
cli: introduce rwctl prefill dry-run and report generator
quant: add guidance heuristics and safe-fallback hooks
tests: add integration tests and CI load harness
review_thread: Diego Ruiz (review): Please add a fallback path when prefill budget computation fails; observed a nil-pointer in staging if tenant metadata is missing.
Asha Menon (author): Added conservative fallback budget and hid nils behind an accessor; added unit test (TestBudgetFallback).
Priya Patel (review): Telemetry tags look good but we should avoid high-cardinality tag explosion for small tenants.
Asha Menon (author): Collapsed tenant dimension into tenant_cohort for low-volume tenants; added sampling to high-cardinality traces.
Marcus Li (review + approval): Verified dry-run outputs and simulated canary rollout; performance numbers look reasonable. Approving.
release_notes: Introduce Frugal Prefill Orchestrator: per-tenant prefill budgets, quantization guidance, rwctl dry-run simulator, telemetry console enrichment; safe canary rollout and automatic fallbacks.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature behind FF; 2) Enable for internal tenants only and run rwctl dry-run for 24h; 3) Canary cohort (5% tenants) for 48h with automated rollback thresholds; 4) Gradually expand to 25/50/100% if metrics stable; 5) Monitor Console "prefill-savings" panel and regression alerts.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: prefill.orchestrator.enabled. CLI: rwctl prefill dry-run --tenant=<id> --simulate-traffic=<profile>. If rollback triggers, set prefill.orchestrator.enabled=false and reapply previous policy via admin console.
motivating_benchmarks: Synthetic tenant sim: projected token reduction 22%-36% depending on cold-start rate; median tail latency increase <3ms for 8-bit profiles in canary runs.
public_notes: Customers: introduces safe cost-optimization defaults that we will offer as a managed opt-in; initial availability limited to Dedicated and Hosted tiers with SLO guardrails.
